opening_message:
Ticket 1: Eric Woods (employee ID E019) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E019.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. As full-time, write is within policy (admin would require owning role; Engineer does not own Payroll). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E019 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: The two team notes about E019 conflict on employment type: the HR note says full-time (which would allow write for Payroll), but the Security note says the Security DB shows contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors with basic training max out at read and cannot be granted write (never admin). Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive interpretation to avoid exceeding the access policy, so write cannot be granted; the maximum allowed is read.
